title: verification
description: research/verifications.json (Implementation Decision 17; ticket 97): the verification of every inherited result, written only by wayline.verification through the ledger, rendered as research/VERIFICATIONS.md, and journaled as `verification`. An inherited result is one inherited Results heading with all its claims judged together; it stands unchecked until every claim has a verdict (verified) or it is found unverifiable, with the reason. Each verdict names its route. `material` is the code, data, and software each result needs that is missing (fetchable data never is), ids M1 onward, with the owner's or the decider's reply; `reads` are the consultant's batched reads of cited claims, one per reference and dossier level.

path.description: the file of the inherited code it is about, project-relative

heading.description: the inherited Results heading: the result's name

claims.description: the inherited claims under it, as first deconstructed

reason.description: why it is unverifiable; null otherwise

disagreements.description: where the inherited Methods and the inherited code disagree on a method or a parameter, found by the parser inventory at setup (ticket 108), which the verification answers

leads.description: the concerns the setup's Sonnet reading of the inherited code raised about a file this result uses, each grep-checked in its file (ticket 108): what the verification looks into

contradictions.description: contradicting pairs attached to the result (ticket 95), which its verification answers

ticket.description: the verification ticket; null for a read code made

commit.description: for reproduced: the commit intake recorded, which it ran at

substitute.description: the substitute data it was reached on, when any: the verdict covers only the claim narrowed to that data

by.description: the finding that replaced the claim

heading.description: the inherited result that needs it

licensed.description: licensed software (MATLAB and its toolboxes): provide, port to Octave, or port to Python

rebuild.description: whether a rebuild (a port or a reimplementation) can work, which makes it the recommended reply

found_by.description: the critic's memo at setup, or the verification ticket that found the gap

level.description: the dossier's level when it was read; a promotion reads it again

failed.description: why the consultant gave no usable answer; the claims are not asked about again at this level
